questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a English speaking country, and a way to explore and live in a different country with good opportunities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UBC was really good with information by mail. I got my courses before I left and felt very well prepared before leaving, and he rest got fixed very easily when i arrived.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a ”buddy" from UBC who I could ask any questions. UBC also made different buddy groups the first day, which you could use during your stay if you wanted to. Otherwise I used the facebook group for students from  Copenhagen University going to Vancouver, where we met before going and helped each other.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was searching for housing with two other danish students, and we looked in all Facebook groups with housing in Vancouver and on other sites, but there were so many for all offers, so you had to be fast. At last, we found a basement suite off-campus, which was really good and we were happy to stay there. There were a lot of opportunities with living off-campus, we could throw parties and it was nice to have school and home seperated.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived 40 minutes by bus from UBC, so a bit far, but you got used to it, and I actually thought it was nice to live somewhere else and get to know that part of the city as well. I lived close to Mainstreet which is a really nice place with lots of restaurants and bars, which I used a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Because of Covid, there weren't spots for all students to live on-campus, so I found it really hard to figure out where to live under the stay, and I could have used some more help to find accommodation.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got a link, where I had to wish courses. I wished for 8 different courses and got 5 of them, and then I chose 4 of them. For me, the registration for courses went really easy and well, and I got the ones I wanted

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always write to UBC office and they replied fast and always did their best to help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the ones I wanted. In the beginning, you have a month where you can change courses if you want, and it is a very easy process. So you can go to a lot of different classes and see which one you want, and then decide finally in October.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All courses have very different exam forms, so take a look at the exams and have in mind what kind of exams you like when you choose courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 300 level courses. Two psychology courses and two sociology courses. I found the sociology courses very easier than the psychology. So 400 level courses would have been fine in sociology

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I only had good professors! They were all very passionated about their courses

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
"Childhood and adolescence" 
"Personality psychology"
"Diversity in Family forms" 
"Social Statistics"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: My experience is that UBC has very good courses in general

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I decided to buy a car, which was not that expensive and totally worth it!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is pretty expensive. Vancouver is in general a pretty expensive city to live in

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of hiking opportunities, which is amazing. From November you can go ski. In Vancouver, you can do all sorts of sports. I joined the pottery club and ski club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Hike and ski, but UBC has so many clubs, so go explore 
UBC also has free swimming, which I used and really enjoyed

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hike and ski!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I didnøt find it hard at all. All Canadians are so sweet and kind, so very easy to get used to the culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In all my courses it was almost only Canadians, so it was a good opportunity to talk with locals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The country is huge, so I had to get used to the distances. That is why I on day 3 bought a car ;)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kind people and the amazing views with mountains and the sea

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't prioritize school, go explore and enjoy being in such a pretty country.
